newsitem.title: GERMANY: German magazines losing more ad money to TV-group.
newsitem.headline: German magazines losing more ad money to TV-group.

text.p: German magazines lost further advertising income to television in 1996, continuing a decade-long trend, the Association of German Periodical Publishers (VDZ) said on Monday.

The VDZ said the magazine industry's net advertising income last year dropped 2.5 percent to 3.42 billion marks while it said the television industry was expected to post modest ad growth for the same period.

"Since the end of the 1980s, magazines have had to fight with electronic media for their share of advertising budgets," the VDZ said in a statement. "Magazines last year showed no sign of a boost, neither in the advertising nor in the distribution markets."
Fiercer market competition has led more and more new magazines to fold, the VDZ said, although the number of magazines in Germany has almost doubled in the last 10 years.
Total magazine circulation has risen by nearly 25 percent during the same period to 128 million, in what the VDZ called the most saturated magazine market in the world.
The association, however, cited data from Nielsen advertising market researchers indicating 4.2 percent growth in magazine advertising during the first quarter of 1997 as grounds for optimism.
